bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42478821 (curl): Heap-use-after-free READ 1 found by fuzz target curl_fuzzer_http [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42478821
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 1` in `seturl` while replaying the exact staged 56-byte `curl_fuzzer_http` TLV witness. Decoding `poc` with the repo's `read_corpus.py` shows three fields: TLV 1 `CURLOPT_URL` with one byte `0xff`, TLV 2 server banner `HTTP/2 383     \nlocatiOn:.#    \n `, and TLV 29 `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` with a nonzero 32-bit value. In `Curl_http_readwrite_headers()`, curl copies the attacker-controlled redirect value `".#"` from that response into request state and, because follow-location is enabled, stores it as `data->req.newurl`. `multi_runsingle()` later feeds that relative redirect into `Curl_follow()`, which calls `curl_url_set(..., CURLUPART_URL, newurl, CURLU_URLENCODE)`. Because the redirect is relative, `curl_url_set()` resolves it against the current URL with `concat_url()`, producing an absolute URL whose path ends in `/.#`. `seturl()` URL-encodes that path into a temporary heap buffer, cuts `fragment` as an interior pointer into the same allocation, and then runs `Curl_dedotdotify()` on the path portion. Dot-segment removal normalizes `/.` to `/`, so the replacement branch frees the old temporary `path` buffer at line 887 while `fragment` still points inside it. The later `if(fragment && fragment[0])` test dereferences that dangling interior pointer at line 934 and matches the saved ASan crash. The fix introduces `u->temppath` and duplicates fragment/query content before any free so those interior aliases are not used after the temporary path buffer is replaced.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled redirect value from the HTTP response. This call materializes the `Location:` header into a standalone string that later drives redirect processing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` decodes to a TLV 2 server banner `HTTP/2 383     \nlocatiOn:.#    \n `. When this header line reaches `Curl_http_readwrite_headers()`, `Curl_copy_header_value()` trims the trailing whitespace and newline and yields the redirect string `".#"`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the temporary encoded path buffer has already been freed, this condition still dereferences the stale `fragment` interior pointer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` here, 11 bytes inside the 25-byte region allocated in `seturl` at line 856 and freed in `seturl` at line 887.

root_cause.description: The old temporary path buffer is freed after dot-segment normalization selects a replacement path, but the earlier `fragment` pointer still aliases storage inside that freed allocation.
root_cause.note: The fix keeps the temporary path under `u->temppath` ownership and copies fragment/query strings before any replacement free, which is the lifetime obligation missing in the vulnerable code.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness's first server banner yields HTTP status 383 and a `Location:` header line, so this redirect-header branch is entered. The same witness also sets `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` nonzero, which lets the parsed redirect continue into the follow path instead of being stored only as informational state.

tainted_value_origin.description: This cloned redirect target is the exact attacker-derived string later moved into `newurl` and reparsed by `Curl_follow()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: For the staged witness, `data->req.location` is `".#"` after `Curl_copy_header_value()` trims the mixed-case `locatiOn:` header.

coarse_trace.summary: The HTTP response parser recognizes a 3xx `Location:` header, copies the attacker-controlled value `".#"`, and stores it in redirect state because follow-location is enabled.
After the response finishes, the redirect branch consumes `data->req.newurl`, marks the operation as `FOLLOW_REDIR`, and calls `Curl_follow()`.
Redirect following reparses the stored redirect through `curl_url_set()` with `CURLU_URLENCODE`, so URL parsing takes the encoded-path path in `seturl()`.
Because the redirect target is relative, `curl_url_set()` resolves `".#"` against the current URL and passes the resulting absolute URL into `parseurl()` and `seturl()`.

The parser allocates a temporary encoded path buffer, takes `fragment` as an interior pointer into it, normalizes away the `/.` dot segment, frees the old buffer, and later reads `fragment[0]`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: Source step. Under the 3xx redirect-header branch, libcurl copies the attacker-controlled `Location:` value out of the first server banner. For the staged witness the banner line is `locatiOn:.#    `, so after whitespace trimming `location` becomes `".#"`.

The parsed redirect string is stored in request state and then cloned into `data->req.newurl` because `data->set.http_follow_location` is nonzero for this witness. That clone is the redirect text later consumed by the follow logic.

When the transfer completes, the redirect branch takes the saved `data->req.newurl`, moves it into local `newurl`, marks the operation as `FOLLOW_REDIR`, and enters `Curl_follow()`. Without `data->req.newurl`, this reparse path is not taken.

The redirect handler reparses the attacker-controlled redirect through the URL API and, because this is a true redirect, passes `CURLU_URLENCODE`. That flag is what makes `seturl()` allocate a temporary encoded path buffer later.

Because the redirect target `part` is relative rather than absolute, `curl_url_set()` resolves it against the current URL already stored in `u`. With the witness value `".#"`, `concat_url()` appends that relative part to the current directory so the reparsed URL's path reaches `seturl()` with a trailing `/.#` dot-segment-plus-fragment form.

With `flags & CURLU_URLENCODE` and a nonempty path from step 5, `seturl()` allocates a temporary heap copy of the path and URL-encodes it in place. The saved ASan allocation stack points to this `malloc()` at line 856.

The parser splits the fragment from the temporary path buffer by writing a NUL over `#` and then advancing `fragment` to an interior pointer within the same allocation. For the resolved `/.#` form, `fragment` points at the empty fragment string stored in the temporary buffer.

After fragment splitting, `Curl_dedotdotify()` normalizes the remaining path. Because step 5 produced a path ending in `/.`, RFC3986 dot-segment removal returns a different string with that `/.` collapsed away, so the replacement branch is taken.

Root-cause step. The old temporary path buffer from step 6 is freed because normalization chose a replacement string, but the earlier `fragment` pointer from step 7 is not duplicated or re-based first. That leaves `fragment` dangling over the freed allocation. The fix adds separate temporary ownership and moves fragment/query copying earlier specifically to avoid this stale interior alias.

Sink. This condition still reads `fragment[0]` after step 9 freed the backing path buffer. The saved ASan report records the resulting 1-byte heap-use-after-free read at this exact line, 11 bytes inside the same 25-byte region allocated in step 6 and freed in step 9.

format.name: curl_fuzzer_http TLV corpus entry with a 3xx `Location: .#` redirect
format.contract: The exact staged 56-byte witness decodes as three TLVs: TLV 1 `CURLOPT_URL` with raw byte `0xff`, TLV 2 server banner `HTTP/2 383     \nlocatiOn:.#    \n `, and TLV 29 `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` with the 4-byte big-endian value `0x20202020`, which is nonzero. The crash-relevant semantics proved by this witness are the 3xx status line, the mixed-case `Location:` header whose trimmed value is exactly `".#"`, and nonzero follow-location, which together drive `Curl_follow()` into `seturl()`'s fragment-handling path and reproduce the saved `heap-use-after-free READ of size 1`.
